title: Pilot study: Investigation of the human bioavailability and elimination of Kukoamin A and B through the consumption of mashed potatoes.
summary:
Kukoamine A and B are found in foods such as potatoes. Studies show that kukoamine A and B can have various health benefits. However, it is not known how well the body can absorb kukoamine A and B from food and how well the body absorbs them. Furthermore, there has been no research into how kukoamin A and B are metabolized in the body and how quickly the two substances are excreted. Due to this lack of data, it is difficult to predict the relevance of the above-mentioned health-promoting effects of kukoamin A and B from food.
We would like to investigate how much kukoamine A and B we can find in the blood and urine of test subjects after they have eaten mashed potatoes. To do this, it is necessary to test the blood and urine for these two substances over several hours. We would also like to find out whether the human body converts kukoamine A and B into other substances.
conditions: Absorption and metabolism of health-promoting plant substances (anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, cell and neuroprotective)

interventions.name: Study meal: Mashed potatoes, single serving, 6 g mashed potatoes/kg body weight

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy subjects aged 18 years and older and women of childbearing age using contraception
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy/breastfeeding; consumption of tomatoes, potatoes, peppers, products made from these foods, or other products containing solanaceous plants in the 24 hours prior to the start of the study; relevant intolerances to potatoes or milk; use of medication; known medical conditions (especially diabetes); existing drug addiction.
